Catholic Liturgy. The formal worship practices of the Roman Catholic Church, centered on the Mass, a ritualistic reenactment and commemoration of Christ's sacrifice. Music is integral to Catholic liturgical practice, serving both practical functions like guiding the congregation through ritual and devotional purposes like inspiring spiritual contemplation. From the medieval period through the present, Catholic liturgical worship has been inseparable from sacred music, spawning entire musical genres and shaping the development of Western classical music.

The Mass consists of ordinary, unchanging parts that recur in each Mass: Kyrie, Gloria, Credo, Sanctus, and Agnus Dei, and proper, changing parts specific to each liturgical day, each with designated liturgical chant. Gregorian chant is the traditional monophonic liturgical music of the Catholic Church, used in the proper and ordinary. The sixth-century codification, attributed to Pope Gregory the First, standardized chants across the Church.

Polyphonic settings of the Mass, composing multiple vocal lines for the ordinary, became a major compositional genre in the Renaissance and Baroque periods. Composers from Palestrina to Mozart wrote masses as their most prestigious sacred works. The responsorial form, cantor and choir antiphon-response, structures much Catholic chant, allowing congregational participation while trained singers elaborate ornamentally. Vespers, evening prayer service, and Lauds, morning prayer service, complement the Mass. Both used chant and polyphony and became vehicles for elaborate musical composition, particularly in the Baroque period.

After the Second Vatican Council from 1962 to 1965, the Latin Mass was largely replaced by Mass in the vernacular, local languages. Many traditional Gregorian chants were simplified or replaced, though traditional Latin Mass still exists in some Catholic communities. Catholic liturgical music influenced not only sacred genres like motet, antiphon, and hymn, but indirectly shaped instrumental music, as composers trained in sacred polyphony applied contrapuntal techniques to secular instrumental forms. Catholic liturgy connects to Gregorian chant, medieval music, the modal system underlying Gregorian chant, sacred music, polyphony, Christianity, and Pope Gregory the First.
